page: Amazon Web Services im4gn.2xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by an ARM64 AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.5 GHz with no hyperthreading. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of memory, providing 4.0 GB per core, and includes a bundled 3750 GB local NVMe SSD. Network connectivity is delivered via a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate average performance across multiple workloads. The server achieves a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1519.78 and a multi-core score of 12131.82. Memory bandwidth is measured at 472.87 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 121.23 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. In database operations, the instance performs reliably, registering 9.97 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and an average score of 5226.37 in Passmark database operations. However, single-threaded performance is weaker, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 937.0 and a poor bzip3 decompression rate of 7.19 GB/sec.

The im4gn.2xlarge offers high resource density for storage-heavy workloads due to its substantial 3750 GB NVMe SSD capacity relative to its 8 vCPUs. This makes it a cost-efficient option for applications requiring high local storage throughput without needing massive compute scaling. However, the ARMv8 architecture lacks AVX and AMX instruction sets, resulting in weaker performance for vector-heavy tasks like LLM inference, where text generation for a 7B model is limited to 6.75 tokens per second. The server is best suited for databases, static web serving, and storage-intensive applications.
